chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Abbas and al-Haytham, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Ali ibn Bashir al-Nabbal, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman during her waiting period without knowing, while she knew that time remained of her waiting period and that he had accused her (of adultery) after his knowledge of that. He said: 'If she knew that what she did was forbidden for her and proceeded to do it, then upon her is the punishment, the punishment of the fornicator, and I do not see anything upon her husband when he accused her. And if she did that out of ignorance on her part, then when he accused her of adultery, the accuser is punished with the limit, and they are separated, and she observes what remained of her first waiting period, and after that she observes a complete waiting period.'
Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever has sexual intercourse with a boy and causes him to ejaculate, his sister, his mother, and his daughter are not permissible for him forever.

key_terms.عِدَّة: Waiting period (Iddah) after divorce or death

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a man who marries a woman during her waiting period if she knew it was forbidden versus if she was ignorant?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the jurisprudential distinction between *jahalah* (ignorance) and *'ilm* (knowledge) in determining the *Hadd* punishment for fornication when a man marries a woman during her *'Iddah*. Al-Sheikh’s appended ruling on *fajr* with a boy establishes a permanent prohibition (*haram abad*) for the boy's mother, sister, and daughter, reflecting the Shia emphasis on sexual acts creating enduring marital barriers beyond mere lineage.
